name: design.brilliant/canvas
title: Brilliant Design (hosted)
description: Design pages, screens and posts on a live, editable Brilliant canvas. No install, no account.

tools.name: get_knowledge
tools.description: Use this when writing Blueprint rows for a Brilliant design: it loads Brilliant's Blueprint and design knowledge pages by key (blueprint/core, blueprint/layout, blueprint/paint, blueprint/text, design/foundations). Each key pulls in its prerequisites unless includeDependencies is false; all loads the whole tree page by page within the response budget.

all.description: Load every page of the tree (the response budget defers the rest by name).

includeDependencies.description: Also load the assumes: prerequisites of each key. Default true.

keys.description: Knowledge keys, each a path under the knowledge tree without .md (blueprint/core).

tools.name: design
tools.description: Use this when the user asks to design, mock up, wireframe or lay out a user interface or a page as an editable design: a website, landing or pricing page, an app screen (login, settings, checkout), a dashboard, a slide, a social post, a poster, an invitation, a menu or a business card, or a design to edit or tweak by hand. It opens a new, empty, live Brilliant canvas in the chat; the design is built there as editable layers (frames, text, shapes, icons). Not for generating a photograph or an illustration, for photo edits (use remove_background) or for questions that need no design. Do not use to change a design already open in this conversation. Rows take literal values (hex colors, numbers); design tokens are not available in this lane.

intent.description: One plain line on what this design is about to hold, such as "A pricing section with three plans and a highlighted middle tier". The canvas shows it beside ChatGPT's cursor while the first rows are written.

title.description: A short name for the design.

tools.name: edit_design
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to change, restyle or add to a Brilliant design opened in this conversation, such as adding a section or a screen next to it, changing the copy or the colors, or making it darker. It takes the design's seed and Blueprint rows and applies them on that design's canvas: new rows add layers, and a row that leads with an id or #ref the design already has changes that layer. It returns how the rows applied, naming any row that did not apply. Its rows run up to 8,000 characters per call; a call of about 20 rows (about 1,500 characters), such as a page's frame and its first section, lands on the canvas within a few seconds. Rows take literal values (hex colors, numbers); design tokens are not available in this lane.

blueprint.description: Readable design rows, one element per line: its kind, text, size and colors in short form. Example: t("Sign in",Inter,15,b) f[(#FFFFFF)] is the bold white 15 px Inter text "Sign in". Children sit indented two spaces under their parent; no file() row; literal values (hex colors, numbers). Placeholder copy shows a person as a role label ("Account owner", "Home cook") rather than a first and last name: a profile, a name field's sample value and a testimonial's author alike. Brilliant applies rows as they arrive and the canvas animates each batch in, so a design reads best when its first rows set the frame and its main sections and later rows fill in the details.

seed.description: The slug of a design opened in this conversation (from the design result).

tools.name: remove_background
tools.description: Use this when the user attaches or links a photo and asks to remove its background, cut out the subject or get a transparent PNG. It returns the user's own photo with the background cut away by a matte, at its original size up to 2,048 pixels on the long edge, every subject pixel unchanged. Do not use to generate a new image. It cuts the subject out of the original photo with a matte. It takes the user's image as image (a file the user attached), imageUrl (https) or imageBase64, and returns the cutout, a share link, and Open in Brilliant.

imageBase64.description: The photo's bytes as base64 (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 25 MB).

imageUrl.description: An https URL of the photo (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 25 MB).

mimeType.description: The mime type of imageBase64 (optional, the bytes are sniffed).

tools.name: place_image
tools.description: Use this when the user wants an image (one they attached, or one generated in this conversation) placed into a Brilliant design opened in this conversation: it puts the image on the canvas as an editable image layer, or as the fill of a target layer, and answers how it applied. It takes the design's seed and the image as image (the file attached or generated in the conversation), imageUrl (https) or imageBase64 (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 25 MB); target names an existing frame or shape by its id or #ref to fill instead.

image.description: The image attached to or generated in the conversation.

imageBase64.description: The image's bytes as base64 (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 25 MB).

imageUrl.description: An https URL of the image (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 25 MB).

name.description: The new image layer's name (default Image).

seed.description: The slug of a design opened in this conversation (from the design result).

target.description: The id or #ref of an existing frame or shape in the design whose fill becomes the image; its size and position stay. Without it, the image lands as a new layer.

tools.name: inspect_design
tools.description: Use this when the user wants to see, check or talk about a Brilliant design opened in this conversation: it returns the element tree as Blueprint rows with ids (the ids rows can target), how each turn of the design ended (complete, halted, stopped at a limit, or still building) and any rows that did not apply. With wait, it holds up to 25 seconds for the design's latest turn to end; a turn still building at that point answers its progress. A design renders once the user has the canvas open in the chat.

seed.description: The design's slug (from the design result).

wait.description: true holds the answer up to 25 seconds for the design's latest turn to end. Default false.
